abstract: The elementary gates are basic building blocks of quantum logic circuit. They should be simple, efficient, and easy to implement. In this article, we propose the ternary controlled X (TCX) gate or the ternary controlled Z (TCZ) gate as the two-qutrit elementary gate, which is universal when assisted by arbitrary one-qutrit gates. Based on Cartan decomposition, we give the one-qutrit elementary gates. Also, we discuss the physical implementation of these elementary gates and show that they are feasible with current technology. Then we investigate the synthesis of some important ternary gates, such as the ternary SWAP gate, ternary Toffoli gates and Muthukrishnan-Stroud gates. Finally we extend these elementary gates to a more general case for qudit systems. This work provides a unified description for the synthesis of both binary and multi-valued quantum circuits.

specification.problem: Reconstruct, from the abstract alone, a mathematical specification of the proposed two-qutrit elementary gates (ternary controlled-X, TCX, and ternary controlled-Z, TCZ), their mutual relation, and a smallest useful synthesis example (the ternary SWAP gate) built from these elementary gates plus one-qutrit gates.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Scope chosen (no experiment_scope supplied): (i) define the qutrit shift/clock operators and the TCX/TCZ gates on two qutrits; (ii) state the Fourier-conjugation relation between TCX and TCZ; (iii) give the Cartan (KAK) structural form of a general one-qutrit gate as background; (iv) synthesize the ternary SWAP gate from three TCX gates and one one-qutrit gate, with the explicit tiny instance |1>|2> -> |2>|1>. Out of scope: the paper's specific one-qutrit elementary gate set derived from Cartan decomposition, synthesis of ternary Toffoli and Muthukrishnan-Stroud gates, physical-implementation analysis, and the qudit (d>3) generalization.

equations.label: Qutrit shift and clock operators
equations.description: Generalized Pauli operators on a single qutrit; arithmetic in the ket label is modulo 3 (exact modular reduction, not integer addition).
equations.justification: Standard Weyl-Heisenberg (generalized Pauli) operators for d=3, needed to define controlled-X/Z gates.

equations.label: Ternary controlled-X (TCX) gate
equations.description: Control qutrit 1 applies the shift X_3 to target qutrit 2 a number of times equal to the control value. The gate has order 3, so its inverse is its square.
equations.justification: The abstract names the TCX gate but does not define it; this is the standard generalized-CX (SUM) convention. The paper may instead use a convention where X (or a transposition X_{jk}) is applied only when the control is in a specific state such as |2>; that choice changes the synthesis equations below.
assumptions: Generalized-CX (SUM gate) convention adopted for TCX.

equations.label: Ternary controlled-Z (TCZ) gate
equations.description: Diagonal two-qutrit phase gate, symmetric under exchange of the two qutrits.
equations.justification: The abstract names the TCZ gate but does not define it; this is the standard generalized-CZ convention consistent with eq_2.
assumptions: Generalized-CZ convention adopted, consistent with eq_2.

equations.label: Fourier relation between TCX and TCZ
equations.description: TCX and TCZ are equivalent up to one-qutrit Fourier gates on the target; this is why either can serve as the two-qutrit elementary gate when arbitrary one-qutrit gates are available.
equations.abstract_quote: we propose the ternary controlled X (TCX) gate or the ternary controlled Z (TCZ) gate as the two-qutrit elementary gate, which is universal when assisted by arbitrary one-qutrit gates
equations.justification: The abstract treats TCX and TCZ as interchangeable elementary gates given free one-qutrit gates; under the conventions of eq_2 and eq_3 the explicit relation is the standard Fourier conjugation (exact equality).

equations.label: Cartan (KAK) form of a one-qutrit gate
equations.description: Any U in U(3) factors as a global phase, two elements of a U(2)-type subgroup acting on a two-level subspace, and a one-parameter Cartan element mixing the remaining level pair (the symmetric space SU(3)/S(U(2)xU(1)) has rank 1).
equations.justification: The abstract states one-qutrit elementary gates are obtained from Cartan decomposition but gives no formulas; this is the generic KAK structure. The paper's actual choice of subgroup pair and resulting elementary gate list is not recoverable from the abstract.
assumptions: Choice of the subgroup K and the Cartan subalgebra direction is one standard option among equivalent ones.

equations.label: Ternary SWAP from three TCX gates and one one-qutrit gate
equations.description: Operators act right-to-left on |a>|b>: |a,b> -> |a,a+b> -> |-b,a+b> -> |-b,a> -> |b,a> (all arithmetic mod 3). The final one-qutrit negation gate F_3^2 is required because, unlike the qubit case, the three-CX circuit alone yields |-b>|a>.
equations.justification: The abstract says the ternary SWAP gate is synthesized from the elementary gates but gives no circuit; this is a valid decomposition under the TCX convention of eq_2, offered as the smallest useful construction. The paper's actual circuit may differ.
assumptions: TCX_{2->1}^{-1} = TCX_{2->1}^2 is counted as elementary (or as two TCX gates).

registers.name: q_1
registers.role: first qutrit (control of TCX_{1->2}); left ket in |a>|b>

registers.name: q_2
registers.role: second qutrit (target of TCX_{1->2}); right ket in |a>|b>

specification.initial_state: Two-qutrit computational basis state |a>|b> with a,b in {0,1,2}; explicit tiny instance |1>|2> (register order q_1 then q_2).

steps.description: Apply the one-qutrit negation F_3^2 on q_1: |-b, a> -> |b, a>; instance |1,1> -> |2,1>, completing SWAP_3. Optionally, replace any TCX by TCZ conjugated with F_3 on the target (eq_4).

specification.measurement: Optional verification only: measure both qutrits in the computational basis {|0>,|1>,|2>}; for input |1>|2> the outcome (2,1) should occur with probability 1 (exact, noiseless).
specification.classical_postprocessing: Compare measured ternary outcomes (a',b') with the expected (b,a); no further processing.
assumptions: No experiment_scope was supplied, so the ternary SWAP synthesis from TCX gates was chosen as the single smallest useful construction with instance |1>|2>.
TCX and TCZ are taken in the generalized (SUM / omega^{ab}) convention; the paper may define them with a control condition on a specific state (e.g. |2>) or with transposition-type X gates.
Arbitrary one-qutrit gates are assumed available, as stated in the abstract.
